name: Gemini CLI
nameMangling: mcp_ is prepended, [^a-zA-Z0-9_\-.:] becomes _, a leading non-letter gets _; over 63 characters the name becomes the first 30 + ... + the last 30 (V, core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts#L722-L750 at v0.65.0). The policy parser splits at the first _ after mcp_, so no _ in server names (V, docs/tools/mcp-server.md#L692)
listChanged: handled, even when the server does not declare the capability (V, core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts#L410-L424). The skeleton's "manual /mcp reload only" came from the docs and is out of date at v0.65.0
notes: gemini mcp add (0.65.0) writes command, args (always, [] when none), env and url, type, headers; it keeps comments and ends the file with no newline (V, recorded). Probe run 27 Oct (`gemini mcp list` with folder trust off, starting a stdio server): both $TOKEN and ${TOKEN} expand in env and args (V). User-level servers are suppressed in an untrusted folder (V, `gemini mcp list` warning). Source (v0.65.0): $VAR, ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expand across the whole settings object (V, cli/src/utils/envVarResolver.ts); a url with no type means streamable HTTP with an SSE fallback, which disagrees with the docs' "bare url means SSE" (V both; tk always writes type); per-server enablement lives in ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json; `gemini mcp add` defaults to project scope (-s user needed). GEMINI_CLI_HOME replaces the home folder, not ~/.gemini (V, core/src/utils/paths.ts#L13-L28); tk does not follow it. System files move with GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.

coverage.note: killed, crashed, hung and timed out hooks all let the call through, run on 0.66.0 and 0.65.0; the extension's policies/tk.toml and the printed user-tier TOML are what hold without the hook; a hook cannot approve; headless, Gemini's own prompt does not pass; under security.environmentVariableRedaction or GITHUB_SHA the hook loses TOKEN-named variables, so tk run also sets GEMINI_CLI_TK_CHAT_TOKEN_FILE (lane I, applied by integration w2)
